Observed sequence: a man in his 30s with type 1 diabetes underwent combined kidney–pancreas transplant. Early delayed renal graft function required one dialysis session then recovered. Immunosuppression consists of tacrolimus, mycophenolate and tapering prednisone with antimicrobial prophylaxis. Trimethoprim‑sulfamethoxazole (TMP‑SMX) 80/400 mg daily was stopped on post‑transplant day 25 because of hyperkalaemia and replaced by pentamidine. TMP‑SMX was restarted on day 69 when serum creatinine was stable at 0.75–0.88 mg/dL and tacrolimus troughs were 5.5–7.5. On days 73–75 the patient experienced weakness and dizziness with home glucose readings of 28, 33 and 36 mg/dL. No paired venous glucose, insulin or C‑peptide was obtained during these episodes. C‑peptide values of 2–3.9 ng/mL were measured at other post‑transplant times, not during the lows. The response to changing prophylaxis is not supplied.

Immediate concern: recurrent severe hypoglycaemia in a pancreas transplant recipient.

Medication‑related hypotheses: tacrolimus can impair insulin clearance; TMP‑SMX may augment sulfonylurea‑like effect or reduce renal clearance of insulin; pentamidine can cause pancreatic β‑cell toxicity and subsequent rebound hyperinsulinaemia. Non‑medication hypotheses: graft pancreatitis, infection, altered counter‑regulatory hormones, or dietary mismatch.

C‑peptide data: values of 2–3.9 ng/mL indicate endogenous insulin secretion at the times sampled, but because they were not drawn during hypoglycaemia they cannot confirm or exclude hyperinsulinaemia as the cause of the lows.

Next clinical assessment: obtain simultaneous venous glucose, insulin and C‑peptide during a hypoglycaemic episode (or via a supervised fast) to determine whether insulin excess is present, and review tacrolimus levels and prophylaxis choice.
